hinge.title: Decide when lime water turning milky is evidence for carbon dioxide and a chemical change.
node_labels: Matter: materials, particles, mixtures and change

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: The new white solid is calcium hydroxide.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: Calcium carbonate makes lime water milky even when it is dissolved.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: Calcium carbonate + water → calcium hydroxide + carbon dioxide

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: Blowing carbon dioxide into plain water turns it milky.

intelligence.enrichment: Carbon dioxide turns lime water milky because calcium hydroxide reacts with carbon dioxide to form insoluble calcium carbonate and water. Carbon dioxide entering lime water causes calcium carbonate to form, and the insoluble calcium carbonate makes the lime water appear milky. The learner explains that carbon dioxide turns lime water milky because it reacts with calcium hydroxide to form insoluble calcium carbonate and water. Any fizzing bubbles from a mixture are carbon dioxide, whether or not lime water turns milky.
